fixed.explanation: _compute_grand_margin looks up aggfunc[k] for every column in data[values], but a dict aggfunc may not contain every column. That raised an uncaught KeyError, since only TypeError was swallowed. The edit skips columns missing from the dict, so margins=True drops the same columns as margins=False. I did not run this, and I did not check the code that uses the returned margin downstream.

query.intent: The grand margin computation in pivot_table iterates over every column in data[values] and indexes aggfunc[k] for each, raising KeyError when aggfunc is a dict lacking that column. It should skip columns not present in the aggfunc dict, matching the non-margins path.
query.symptom: pivot_table with margins=True and a dict aggfunc that doesn't cover all value columns raises KeyError, whereas margins=False silently drops the uncovered columns.

history.analysis: _compute_grand_margin iterates over data[values] and indexes aggfunc[k]. It only catches TypeError, so a dict aggfunc without key k raises KeyError. This is the code the issue names, and the fix is to skip columns missing from the dict.
